text:
kate: quick heads upour nextjs edge onboard sample is failing only after adapter bundling. runtime: \"TypeError: Class extends value undefined\". local node dev server fine.
kate: repro and minimal configs in the repo.
kate: package.json snippet:
```\n{\n  \"name\": \"rw-onboard-edge\",\n  \"type\": \"module\",\n  \"exports\": { \"import\": \"./dist/sdk.mjs\", \"require\": \"./dist/sdk.cjs\" }\n}\n```
kate: tsconfig.json snippet:
```\n{\n  \"compilerOptions\": {\n    \"target\": \"ES2020\",\n    \"module\": \"ESNext\",\n    \"moduleResolution\": \"bundler\",\n    \"declaration\": true,\n    \"isolatedModules\": true\n  }\n}\n```
drew: bundlers/adapters often inline small CJS compat shims. if you have a runtime guard like `if (typeof exports === 'object') module.exports = require(...)` the adapter can rewrite it and end up with undefined. that matches the class extends symptom.
hugo: also check for polyfills pulled by the shimwe've seen \"self is not defined\" from a fallback injected into the bundle.
molly: i hit this last week. for edge-targeted samples the safest approach is ESM-only artifacts. the sample should import the mjs directly (or set exports.import only) so adapters don't touch the cjs path.
drew: +1. also try switching the sample tsconfig.moduleResolution to `node16` instead of `bundler`. bundler resolution sometimes causes export-map rewrites that confuse adapters.
hugo: on typing DXour SDK currently exposes a generic like `request<T = unknown>(...)`. that's strict but JS sample authors get `unknown` back with no completion. pragmatic pattern: provide a JS-friendly overload first, then the generic overload. e.g.
```ts
request(path: string, body?: any): Promise<Record<string, any>>;
request<T = unknown>(path: string, body?: unknown): Promise<T>;
```
that gives vanilla JS people helpful autocomplete while TS users can opt-in.
molly: also add small helper methods on the client for ergonomics: `client.json<T = any>(...)` and `client.raw(...)` or `client.withType<T>()`. samples can show both.
kate: we tried enabling `esModuleInterop` in the sample tsconfig and it fixed the runtime in one adapter, but broke several overload inference tests in CI. toggling compiler flags is noisy.
drew: prefer not to flip consumer-facing compiler flags. instead land the sample export change (ESM-only) + helper APIs in SDK so inference stays stable.
hugo: plus a small post-build check: after building the sample, run a quick node import of `dist/sdk.mjs` and assert the exported class is constructible. that would've caught it earlier.
molly: agreed. and add a lightweight PR CI job that builds the sample as ESM and runs it in a local edge adapter (vercel dev or deno) as a smoke test.
drew: devx-bot can you open a ticket for the smoke CI and assign to @kate?
devx-bot: created issue #1701: \"devex: build ESM-only onboarding sample + edge adapter smoke test\" with labels devex/ci and priority/medium. assigned to @kate.
kate: thanks. my immediate plan: 1) change sample package.json to import-only ESM (or import the mjs directly), 2) switch sample tsconfig.moduleResolution to node16, 3) remove conditional CJS runtime shim from sample artifacts, 4) add `client.json`/`client.raw` helpers in SDK and a short README example showing `await client.request<{embedding:number[]}>(...)` and the JS `await client.json('/embed', {q})`, 5) add the post-build constructibility test and the CI smoke job.
hugo: when you update the typings please include a tiny TS example in the PR description so reviewers can validate inference improvements.
molly: and add a 1-line changelog: \"samples: prefer ESM-only artifacts for edge adapters; add JS-friendly typing overloads and helpers.\"
kate: will open the PR and ping when CI green. thanks all for the quick triage.
